h: Prayer, the Patriarchs, and the Voice of Yaakov
The Work of Faith and Divine Service
The Daily Blessings and the Duty of Prayer

p: בְּתַנְחוּמָא רֵישׁ פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ: "יְלַמְּדֵנוּ רַבֵּינוּ: כַּמָּה בְּרָכוֹת מִתְפַּלֵּל אָדָם בְּכָל יוֹם? וְכוּלֵי", וְהֶאֱרִיךְ בָּזֶה

. In Midrash Tanchuma at the beginning of this parashah (Vayera 1): "Let our master teach us: How many blessings does a person pray each day? etc.," and the Midrash elaborates at length on the laws and praises of prayer.

וְלִכְאוֹרָה אֵין לוֹ שׁוּם שַׁיָּיכוּת לְפָרָשָׁה זוֹ, רַק מַה שֶּׁסִּיֵּים: "תֵּדַע שֶׁכָּל דְּרָכָיו חֶסֶד וְכוּלֵי, וּבְאֶמְצָעִיתָהּ בִּקֵּר אֶת הַחוֹלֶה וְכוּלֵי", וְזֶה אֵין לוֹ קִישּׁוּר לְעִנְיַן הַתְּפִלָּה

. Seemingly, this opening discourse on prayer has no connection whatsoever to our parashah, except for how it concludes at the very end: "Know that all His ways are lovingkindness—at the beginning of the Torah He clothed the naked, in its middle He visited the sick ('And Hashem appeared to him'), and at its end He buried the dead," which itself has no apparent link to the topic of prayer!
אַךְ הָעִנְיָן שֶׁבְּפָרָשָׁה זוֹ מָצָאנוּ תְּפִלָּה רִאשׁוֹנָה שֶׁהִתְפַּלֵּל אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם עַל סְדוֹם
: However, the inner connection is that in this parashah we find the very first prayer in the Torah—the prayer that Abraham our father, peace be upon him, prayed on behalf of Sodom:
שֶׁדּוֹרוֹת הָרִאשׁוֹנִים לֹא יָדְעוּ כְּלָל עִנְיַן תְּפִלָּה שֶׁיִּתְפַּלֵּל אָדָם לְשַׁנּוֹת הַגְּזֵירָה
, for the earliest generations did not know the concept of prayer at all—that a human being can pray before God to alter a heavenly decree;
וְנֹחַ שֶׁשָּׁמַע שֶׁעָתִיד הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְהָבִיא מַבּוּל לָעוֹלָם לֹא עָלָה עַל דַּעְתּוֹ לְהִתְפַּלֵּל לְבַטֵּל הַגְּזֵירָה
; thus Noah, even when he heard that the Holy One, blessed be He, was about to bring a flood to destroy the world, never thought to pray to annul the decree;
וְאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ, כֵּיוָן שֶׁגִּילָּה לוֹ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ עוֹנֶשׁ סְדוֹם, הִתְפַּלֵּל עֲלֵיהֶם
. whereas Abraham our father, as soon as Hashem, blessed be He, disclosed to him the impending punishment of Sodom, immediately stood in prayer on their behalf.

Nefesh HaChayim, Gate II, chapter 11, paragraphs 1–4: “Just as a soldier casts aside all his own affairs and needs and willingly gives his life solely for the king's honor, so that the royal crown of that country should be magnified and its sovereignty exalted, so it is most fitting for an upright person to direct all his intention and the purity of his thought in prayer solely toward adding strength to the holy worlds, awakening through his voice the supernal voice to draw from it blessings and illumination for all, removing the spirit of impurity from the world, and having the world perfected under His blessed sovereignty—rather than toward his own affairs and needs at all.

We can see this in the wording of the Rosh Hashanah prayer, which is arranged from beginning to end solely concerning the honor of His blessed sovereignty, that it be exalted as it was originally, before Adam's sin. The same applies to the wording of prayer throughout the year: although on its apparent plain meaning almost all of it is arranged around our own needs, it is certainly clear to every understanding person, and established by its own context, that the Men of the Great Assembly did not intend only the apparent plain meaning of the words, as explained above in chapter 10.

Prayers were instituted corresponding to the daily offerings, which were burnt offerings consumed entirely by the altar fires: all ascended on high, with no ordinary person's portion in them at all.

Although it is an established law in the Talmud that an individual may introduce a new request into his prayer concerning his own needs and distress, in each blessing according to its subject, even in this his ultimate intention should not be directed toward his own distress; that is not the proper path for the upright in heart.”

), And even regarding Abraham himself, it is stated in the holy Zohar (Toldot 137b) that we never find that he prayed to have children, and only regarding Isaac is it written: "And Isaac entreated Hashem opposite his wife, because she was barren" (Genesis 25:21);
וְאַף דְּאָמַר: "הֵן לִי לֹא נָתַתָּה זָרַע" (שָׁם טו, ג), "הַהוּא לָאו בְּגִין צְלוֹתָא הֲוֵי וְכוּלֵי
"; and even though Abraham said, "Behold, to me You have given no seed" (Genesis 15:3), the Zohar states: "that was not by way of prayer, etc.";
וְאַף שֶׁאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ הִתְפַּלֵּל עַל סְדוֹם (וְעַל אֲבִימֶלֶךְ), הָיָה בִּשְׁבִיל אֲחֵרִים, אֲבָל לְהִתְפַּלֵּל עַל עַצְמוֹ לֹא עָלָה עַל דַּעְתּוֹ
. for although Abraham our father prayed on behalf of Sodom (and Abimelech), that was strictly to intercede for others, whereas to pray for his own personal needs did not enter his mind.
וּתְפִלָּה הוּא חֵלֶק יִשְׂרָאֵל, כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "כִּי מִי גוֹי גָּדוֹל אֲשֶׁר לוֹ אֱלֹהִים קְרֹבִים אֵלָיו כַּה' אֱלֹהֵינוּ בְּכָל קָרְאֵנוּ אֵלָיו" (דְּבָרִים ד, ז

); For the power of prayer is the unique portion of Israel, as it is stated: "For what great nation is there that has God so nigh unto them, as Hashem our God is whenever we call upon Him?" (Deuteronomy 4:7);
וְאַף שֶׁהִתְפַּלֵּל שְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם: "וְגַם אֶל הַנָּכְרִי אֲשֶׁר לֹא מֵעַמְּךָ יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא וְגוֹמֵר" (מְלָכִים א ח, מא

), and even though King Solomon, peace be upon him, prayed at the dedication of the Temple: "Moreover, concerning the foreigner who is not of Your people Israel... when he shall come and pray toward this house, hear in heaven" (I Kings 8:41-43),
הַיְינוּ שֶׁיִּשְׁמַע הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מִפְּנֵי קִידּוּשׁ הַשֵּׁם, כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר שָׁם: "לְמַעַן יֵדְעוּן כָּל עַמֵּי הָאָרֶץ אֶת שְׁמֶךָ וְגוֹמֵר

", that is specifically so that Hashem, blessed be He, should answer for the sake of the sanctification of His Name, as is stated explicitly there: "in order that all the peoples of the earth may know Your Name to fear You, as do Your people Israel",
וְרַק הָאָבוֹת הֵם שֶׁחִדְּשׁוּ הַתְּפִלָּה, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בְּרָכוֹת כו:): "תְּפִלּוֹת אָבוֹת תִּקְּנוּם
", whereas intrinsic prayer was innovated solely by the Patriarchs, as our Sages taught (Berakhot 26b): "The Patriarchs instituted the daily prayers,"
וְאַבְרָהָם וְיִצְחָק נִקְרְאוּ גַּם כֵּן יִשְׂרָאֵל כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה רֵישׁ פָּרָשַׁת תּוֹלְדוֹת סג, א
). since Abraham (after his circumcision) and Isaac were also called by the name Israel, as stated in Bereishit Rabbah (beginning of Parashat Toldot, 63:1).

paragraphs.text: Bereshit Rabbah 50:10: ““And it was as dawn broke, the angels urged Lot, saying: Arise; take your wife, and your two daughters who are present, lest you be destroyed in the iniquity of the city” (Genesis 19:15). “And it was as dawn broke, the angels urged Lot, saying” – Rabbi Ḥanina said: [During the interval] from the first gleam of dawn until the illumination of the [entire] eastern horizon, a person can walk four mil; from the illumination of the eastern horizon until sunrise, [he can likewise walk] four mil, as it is stated: “As dawn broke, [the angels urged Lot]” and it is written: “The sun emerged upon the earth [as Lot arrived in Tzo’ar]” (Genesis 19:23). Now, was it really four mil from Sodom to Tzo’ar? Rabbi Ze’eira said: The angel was leveling the way before them. From where is it derived that from the first gleam of dawn until the illumination of the eastern horizon a person can walk four mil? “As [kemo],” “and it was as [ukhmo]” – one period is equal to the other period. Rabbi Yosei bar Avin said: If a person says to you that the morning star is the first gleam of dawn he is saying an untruth. Sometimes it occurs in less time and sometimes it occurs in more time. It is, rather, like two rays of light that ascend in the east and illuminate the world. “And your two daughters who are present [nimtzaot]…” – Rabbi Toviya bar Rabbi Yitzḥak: Two [great] finds [metziot] [would emerge from his daughters] – Ruth the Moavitess and Naama the Amonitess. Rabbi Yitzḥak said: “I found David My servant” (Psalms 89:21) – where did I find him? It was in Sodom.”

paragraphs.text: Tzidkat HaTzadik 222:1: “Then he comes to the attribute of our father Yaakov, in truth and faith, strengthening his faith in Hashem that He will certainly save and that everything is for the good, which is complete truth. This joins the two attributes of Avraham and Yitzchak: fear in the present, and confidence and joy for the future. His prayer is then called “encounter,” as explained at the beginning of the chapter Tefillas HaShachar. This is as I heard concerning the expressions “one who importunes in prayer” and “we have no one to importune,” and in the first chapter of Taanis 8a concerning “He commands it through an intercessor”: It means someone who presses his plea and refuses in any way to turn away and leave Hashem until He answers him, like one who seizes His garment and says, “I will not let You go.” This is the prayer of the night, at the time of complete darkness, after he sees that he has not been answered twice, even though he prayed with love and fear and also with a broken heart. He must press his plea until an answer is compelled, attaining through the attribute of faith the attribute of truth: the clarification visible to the eye that things are indeed as he trusts in his faith.”

, And the fullest perfection of prayer is realized in Jacob, as it is written: "The voice (
הַקֹּל
) is the voice (
קוֹל
) of Jacob" (Genesis 27:22)—meaning the voice of Jacob cries out in the synagogues in prayer, as expounded in the Midrash (Bereishit Rabbah 65:20),
וְזֶה: "הַקֹּל" (חָסֵר ו') – קַל ה' (מַלְכוּת, דִּבּוּר), "קוֹל" (מָלֵא ו') – קוֹל ו' (תִּפְאֶרֶת, יַעֲקֹב, יִחוּד קוֹל וְדִבּוּר
). which is alluded to in the spelling of the two words: the first
הַקֹּל
is spelled defective without a Vav, denoting the voice of the final Hei (Malchut / Speech), while the second
קוֹל
is spelled full with a Vav, denoting the supernal Voice of Vav (Tiferet / Jacob), uniting Kol and Dibbur in prayer.

וּבְפָרָשָׁה זוֹ כְּתִיב: "וַיַּשְׁכֵּם אַבְרָהָם בַּבֹּקֶר אֶל הַמָּקוֹם אֲשֶׁר עָמַד שָׁם אֶת פְּנֵי ה'" (בְּרֵאשִׁית יט, כז), שֶׁמִּזֶּה נִלְמַד בַּגְּמָרָא (בְּרָכוֹת כו:) שֶׁתִּיקֵּן אַבְרָהָם תְּפִלַּת שַׁחֲרִית, וְהַתְּפִלָּה הָרִאשׁוֹנָה שֶׁהִתְפַּלֵּל אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ הָיָה עַל סְדוֹם

. And in this parashah it is written: "And Abraham rose early in the morning to the place where he had stood before Hashem" (Genesis 19:27), from which the Gemara (Berakhot 26b) derives that Abraham instituted the morning prayer (Shacharit), referring back to the first prayer that Abraham our father prayed on behalf of Sodom ("And Abraham remained standing before Hashem").

וְדָוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַתְּפִלָּה, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "וַאֲנִי תְפִלָּה" (תְּהִלִּים קט, ד), וְהָיָה שְׁלִיחַ צִבּוּר שֶׁל כְּלַל יִשְׂרָאֵל
; And King David, peace be upon him, is the very root of prayer, as it is stated: "And I am prayer" (Psalms 109:4), serving as the quintessential emissary of prayer for the entirety of Israel;
וְעַל כֵּן פָּתַח הַמִּדְרָשׁ תַּנְחוּמָא פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ מֵעִנְיַן הַתְּפִלָּה
. and for this reason Midrash Tanchuma opened this parashah with the subject of prayer.
